lessons_to_add.title: The Rook
lessons_to_add.description: Learn how rooks move in straight lines, how they capture, and why open files matter.

steps.title: How the Rook Moves
steps.body_md:
Rooks move any number of squares **horizontally** or **vertically**.

**Key rules:**
- Rooks move in straight lines (files and ranks)
- They **cannot jump** over pieces
- Capturing works by landing on an enemy piece square

steps.title: Blocking
steps.body_md:
Sliding pieces (rook/bishop/queen) cannot move through other pieces.

If something is in the way, the rook must stop before it.

steps.title: Capture with the Rook
steps.body_md: Capture the black pawn on e7 with your rook.
steps.explain_correct_md: Nice! The rook captured by moving straight up the file.
steps.explain_wrong_md: Move the rook from e1 to e7 in a straight line to capture the pawn.
hints: Capture by landing on the pawn's square

quiz.question: Which directions can a rook move?
quiz.explainMd: Rooks move any number of squares horizontally or vertically, but never diagonally.

lessons_to_add.title: The Bishop
lessons_to_add.description: Learn diagonal movement and why bishops stay on the same colour squares forever.

steps.title: How the Bishop Moves
steps.body_md:
Bishops move any number of squares **diagonally**.

**Key rules:**
- Bishops move diagonally only
- They **cannot jump** over pieces
- A bishop always stays on the same colour square (light or dark)

steps.title: Same Colour Forever
steps.body_md:
This bishop is on a dark square, so it can only ever land on dark squares.

That’s why each side starts with **one light-square bishop** and **one dark-square bishop**.

steps.title: Capture Diagonally
steps.body_md: Capture the black pawn on g7 with your bishop.
steps.explain_correct_md: Perfect! Bishops capture diagonally by landing on the target square.
steps.explain_wrong_md: Move the bishop along the diagonal from d4 to g7.
hints: Follow the diagonal line to g7

quiz.question: Can a bishop ever change the colour of square it sits on?

options.text: Yes, if it moves far enough

quiz.explainMd: A bishop always stays on the same colour because diagonal moves preserve square colour.

lessons_to_add.title: The Queen
lessons_to_add.description: Learn the queen’s movement: like a rook and bishop combined.

steps.title: Queen = Rook + Bishop
steps.body_md:
The queen is the most powerful piece.

She moves like a **rook** and a **bishop** combined:
- Any number of squares horizontally/vertically
- Any number of squares diagonally

Like other sliding pieces, she **cannot jump** over pieces.

steps.title: Queen Capture
steps.body_md: Capture the black pawn on d7 with your queen.
steps.explain_correct_md: Great! The queen captured by moving straight up (like a rook).
steps.explain_wrong_md: Move the queen from d4 to d7 (same file) to capture the pawn.
hints: Queen moves like a rook or bishop
d4 to d7 is a straight vertical line

quiz.question: The queen moves like which pieces combined?
quiz.explainMd: The queen combines rook movement (straight lines) and bishop movement (diagonals).

lessons_to_add.title: The King
lessons_to_add.description: Learn how the king moves, what check means, and what moves are illegal.

steps.title: How the King Moves
steps.body_md:
The king moves **one square** in any direction.

**Key rule:** The king is not allowed to move into **check** (a square attacked by an enemy piece).

steps.title: What is Check?
steps.body_md:
Your king is in **check** if an enemy piece attacks the king’s square.

When in check, you must respond immediately by:
- Moving the king
- Capturing the attacking piece
- Blocking the attack (if possible)

steps.title: Escape Check
steps.body_md: Your king is in check from the rook. Move the king to a safe square.
steps.explain_correct_md: Well done! The king moved to a square not attacked by the rook.
steps.explain_wrong_md: Move the king to a square that is not attacked by the rook on e1 (try f3).
hints: Avoid squares attacked by the rook
Try moving diagonally away to f3

quiz.question: Is the king allowed to move into a square attacked by an enemy piece?

options.text: Yes, if it is a good move

quiz.explainMd: The king cannot move into check. Any move that places the king on an attacked square is illegal.

lessons_to_add.title: Castling
lessons_to_add.description: Learn the special king-and-rook move that improves king safety and activates a rook.

steps.title: What is Castling?
steps.body_md:
Castling is a special move that moves the **king** and **rook** at the same time.

**Why castle?**
- Makes your king safer
- Activates your rook toward the center

Kingside castling (O-O): King moves **two squares** toward the rook, rook jumps over to the other side.

steps.title: When Castling is Legal
steps.body_md:
You can castle only if:
- The king and rook have **not moved**
- Squares between them are **empty**
- The king is **not in check**
- The king does **not pass through** check
- The king does **not land in** check

steps.title: Castle Kingside
steps.explain_correct_md: Nice! You castled kingside: king to g1 and rook to f1.
steps.explain_wrong_md: Castle kingside by moving your king from e1 to g1 (two squares).
hints: Move king two squares toward the rook
From e1 to g1 is kingside castling

quiz.question: Can you castle while your king is in check?
quiz.explainMd: You cannot castle out of check. The king must not be in check before castling.
